title: Dynamic throttle & pacing: micro-batch thresholds and KV-cache granularity to avoid OOMs at QPS spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-QPS scenarios we observe sudden tail OOMs on dedicated GPU pools even though average batch sizes remain within expected limits. Root cause investigation suggests a cascade: transient QPS spikes increase concurrent request arrivals -> continuous batching grows batch sizes and KV cache pinned entries (hot shards) -> eviction churn and per-request KV loads increase peak memory usage beyond headroom.

This ticket scopes design + implementation of a dynamic throttle and pacing system that: 1) computes safe micro-batching thresholds per-GPU and per-model using real-time memory accounting and recent sequence-length distributions; 2) applies admission-control/backpressure (soft and hard) to shape incoming QPS to the runtime's safe envelope; 3) makes KV cache eviction and shard-granularity policies adapt to transient pressure to avoid thrashing; 4) provides observability signals and a staged rollout plan.

Goals: reduce OOM incidence to zero for known spikes, maintain P99 latency SLAs within 1.5x baseline where feasible, and avoid manual operator intervention during incident windows.

Non-goals: global architectural refactor of the serving runtime (this is an incremental control-layer + heuristics work).
updates: 2026-02-12: Created ticket after postmortem for incident #INC-2026-17. Initial notes and hypothesis collected from on-call logs.

2026-02-18: Reproduced OOM locally with synthetic QPS driver (see perf-run-2026-02-18). Observed batch size growth from median 8 -> 40 in 6s under bursty arrival pattern. KV cache hit ratio rose from 82% -> 96% but eviction churn doubled memory pressure.

2026-02-22: Spiked two alternative approaches in a branch: (A) strict hard cap on microbatch size + admission queue with 429-on-overflow; (B) adaptive soft-throttling using token-buckets per-GPU that slows acceptance while allowing graceful degradation. Benchmarks show (A) avoids OOMs but increases P99 by ~40% for affected requests; (B) reduces OOMs and keeps P99 within 1.2x but requires accurate headroom estimation.

2026-02-27: Prototype headroom estimator implemented (gpu-memory-accounting/v0). Uses live model-resident memory + estimated KV working set from recent unique-prefix counts. Early tests show headroom predictability within ±12% for steady workloads, wider error under multi-tenant mixing.

2026-03-01: Design review with Runtime and Platform teams. Decision: implement multi-tiered strategy - 1) conservative hard caps per-GPU per-model (safety net), 2) primary adaptive token-bucket admission controller using headroom estimator, 3) KV-cache hot-shard smoothing: switch hot-shard eviction policy to LFU-decay during pressure windows to reduce eviction churn, 4) expose metrics and an opt-in rollout flag for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-05: Started work on runtime patch: admission controller shim + metric hooks. Blocker: need finalized memory-accounting API from infra (ENG-9078). Raised dependency and created follow-up ENG-9240 to complete API work.
2026-03-05: Added A/B experiment plan and dashboards (see links).
acceptance_criteria: 1) No OOMs observed in synthetic 10-minute QPS spike test (5k qps) across 3 GPU instance types; 2) P99 latency increase <= 1.5x baseline for >95% of routes; 3) New metrics surfaced: batch_size_dist, headroom_estimate, kv_eviction_churn; 4) Rollout plan and feature flag ready for dedicated pools.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive throttling could materially impact customer experience. Mitigation: staged rollout, canary traffic at 1% then 5% then 25%; realtime rollback via feature flag. Risk: headroom estimator mispredicts under multi-tenant skew. Mitigation: conservative safety margin + fallback to per-GPU hard cap. Risk: KV policy change may alter cache hit ratios. Mitigation: metric gated A/B test and ability to revert to LRU.
next_steps: 1) Unblock ENG-9078 memory API and wire into admission controller (owner: infra). 2) Finish PR for token-bucket admission controller and LFU-decay hot-shard eviction. 3) Create staging experiment and run 3 stress tests across instance types. 4) Prepare runbook and rollback procedures; coordinate with SRE for on-call support during rollout.
notes: Avoid coupling to model architecture assumptions; estimator should be model-agnostic and driven by observed sequence-length and kv-access patterns. Prefer soft-fallbacks where possible to avoid cascading 429 storms.
